Description: A person's name in any language. The name must consist of one or more parts separated by spaces, hyphens, or apostrophes. Each part must contain at least one letter (Unicode letter), and may also contain combining marks, digits? No digits are allowed in names. Only letters, combining marks, hyphens, apostrophes, and spaces are allowed. The name cannot start or end with a hyphen, apostrophe, or space. Consecutive hyphens, apostrophes, or spaces are not allowed. However, an apostrophe may appear inside a part (e.g., O'Connor) and a hyphen may appear between parts (e.g., Jean-Luc). Spaces separate parts. The entire string must consist only of Unicode letters, combining marks, spaces, hyphens, and apostrophes, and must not have leading/trailing spaces or separators. But hyphen cannot follow apostrophe directly? Actually, we want to disallow any separator immediately after another separator. So the string is composed of one or more 'words' separated by single spaces, hyphens, or apostrophes, where each 'word' is a sequence of letters and combining marks.
